claims.quote: No evidence of contact or interference with the CNG cylinder on that customer’s unit was identified at that time; however, The Heil Co. initiated an investigation to evaluate the potential for cylinder-to-bolt contact.

events.quote: In November 2025 Heil learned that a ladder mounting bracket may have been assembled with a bolt longer than specified in one leg of the ladder support structure on a customer unit.
The longer bolt reduced the designed clearance between the bolt and an adjacent CNG cylinder.

No evidence of contact or interference with the CNG cylinder on that customer’s unit was identified at that time; however, The Heil Co. initiated an investigation to evaluate the potential for cylinder-to-bolt contact.
Inspection identified surface blemishes on seven (7) cylinders in an area corresponding to the location of the ladder mounting bolt.
Measurements of the observed blemishes were evaluated against the cylinder manufacturer's damage assessment criteria and were determined to be within repairable limits.
The Heil Co. continued its investigation to determine the mechanism by which the observed blemishes could occur.
The investigation considered both original vehicle assembly and subsequent service activities.

The investigation determined that installation of an incorrect bolt at one particular location during vehicle assembly or during subsequent service and inspection activities could reduce the intended clearance between the ladder structure and the cylinder.
The investigation continued through July and early August 2026.

Based on the investigation findings, The Heil Co. concluded that an incorrect bolt could potentially be installed in the affected location and could reduce the designed clearance to the adjacent CNG cylinder, creating the potential for cylinder contact and damage.
To eliminate the possibility of incorrect bolt installation at this location, The Heil Co. implemented a design change on August 4, 2026, removing the ladder support leg containing the subject bolt .
On August 11, 2026, The Heil Co. determined that the condition described above constituted a safety- related defect and decided to conduct a voluntary safety recall.
With the exception of the 14 vehicles inspected as described above, there have been no other warranty claims, customer complaints, or field reports on this issue.
Between February and March 2026, The Heil Co. removed and inspected CNG cylinders from fourteen (14) customer vehicles equipped with the same ladder configuration.

CCRG initially assessed that the condition would be overt, progressive, and easily detectable to the customer.
CCRG continued its evaluation and in August 2026 ultimately determined that the loose condition may not be detectable from inside the cabin.

events.quote: On July 13, 2026, and July 30, 2026, Altec received reports from vehicle owners regarding improper operation of the boom stow auto-neutral functionality.
Altec opened an 8D investigation to determine the root cause and identify potentially affected units.
On August 10, 2026, Altec initiated a potential field action investigation after the 8D indicated that additional units in the field may have the same condition.
The investigation evaluated the reported condition, identified units that could be affected, and reviewed production records to determine other owners with units equipped with the same functionality.
On September 25, 2026, after reviewing the investigation results, Altec determined that a field campaign was necessary to address affected units in the field.
In addition to the July warranty claim, there were no other warranty claims or field reports identified.
On July 13, 2026, and July 30, 2026, Altec received reports from vehicle owners regarding improper operation of the boom stow auto-neutral functionality.

events_excluded.sentence: There have been no accidents, injuries or deaths related to this issue.

events.quote: Based on the field information and technical evidence then available, MBAG had identified two factors associated with the condition: climatic exposure and a particular vehicle production period.
The available field data indicated that the reported cases were concentrated in particular climatic regions and within that production period.
MBAG therefore defined the original recall population using those factors.
Following the decision to conduct a recall, MBAG continued monitoring field performance of the front brake hoses, including vehicles both within and outside the original recall population.

Between March and August 2025, MBAG received additional field reports from markets outside the United States involving vehicles produced outside the original recall production range and, in some instances

These reports presented information that was not reflected in the data available when the original recall population was determined and prompted MBAG to reassess whether the condition might extend beyond the originally identified production period and climatic regions.

During September and October 2025, MBAG reviewed the additional reports and available vehicle and production information to determine the appropriate means of obtaining and analyzing representative field parts.

During September and October 2025, MBAG reviewed the additional reports and available vehicle and production information to determine the appropriate means of obtaining and analyzing representative field parts.
In November 2025, MBAG began coordinating a dedicated Field Engineering Activity to obtain additional brake hoses from vehicles exhibiting the reported condition.
From November 2025 through February 2026, MBAG identified candidate vehicles and markets, developed the collection protocol, and coordinated the retrieval and shipment of the requested components.
By June 2026, the requested brake hose components had been collected and returned to MBAG.
MBAG forwarded the components to the supplier for detailed technical analysis and testing.
In July 2026, MBAG reviewed and discussed the results of the supplier’s laboratory and durability testing for the retrieved field parts.

Based on the additional field reports, the analysis of the retrieved components, and the resulting laboratory and durability testing, MBAG reassessed the affected vehicle population with respect to production range and climatic restrictions.
As a result, MBAG identified an expanded vehicle scope covering vehicles produced up to the implementation of a modified brake hose design in series production.
MBAG subsequently identified the potentially affected vehicles in the field.
On September 25, 2026, MBAG determined that a potential safety risk cannot be ruled out for the expanded vehicle population and decided to expand the recall.
This recall expands upon the vehicle population subject to Recall No. 25V116, filed on February 24, 2025.
The Field Engineering Activity was formally launched in March 2026.

events_excluded.sentence: Please refer to the Chronology submitted with that recall report.
In the United States, MBAG is aware of three reports involving vehicles in the expanded recall population, dated 04/02/2026, 05/29/2026 and 08/10/2026.
MBAG is not aware of any cases of crashes, injuries, or property damage related to this condition in the expanded recall population.

events.quote: Volvo Cars received in September 2025 information concerning a potential issue with the head restraint cushion attachment.

Based on this, Volvo together with the supplier, initiated internal investigations to assess the reported information, evaluation of the existing attachment design and consideration of measures to improve its robustness.
The matter was subsequently escalated through the Critical Concern Action Process (CCAP), where a technical investigation and risk assessment were conducted.
On 30 September 2026, the concern was classified as critical, and on 07
October 2026 Volvo Cars decided to prepare a recall after determining that the condition could increase the risk to motor vehicle safety.

events_excluded.sentence: Volvo Cars centrally has not received any reports alleging injuries or fatalities related to this condition.

cause.label: cause stated
cause.quote: Volvo Cars investigations have identified that the head restraint cushion may under certain circumstances, such as very high speed in combination with multiple direction impacts, detach due to insufficient fastening.
